children: Imperial Oil reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of C$16.18B and net income of C$2.45B, with diluted EPS of C$5.11. Revenue and earnings increased from the prior-year quarter as higher crude realizations and refining margins supported results.
Revenue was C$16.18B, compared with C$11.99B in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 34.9%.
Net income was C$2.45B, compared with C$539M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 355.3%.
Diluted EPS was C$5.11, compared with C$1.07 in the prior-year quarter.
Upstream production declined at Kearl and Syncrude over the first nine months. Third-quarter output was also affected by a pipeline outage and a planned Cold Lake turnaround.
Refinery throughput fell to 381,000 barrels per day from 425,000 a year earlier, reflecting downtime, a pipeline outage and turnaround work. Product sales increased on higher exports.
Improved industry refining and polyethylene margins lifted segment results, while renewable diesel product mix also benefited results.
Imperial said trade measures are expected to have no material impact and plans to accelerate share purchases, subject to changing plans and market conditions.
